title: Derived tensor-Hom adjunction for a perfect complex
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let A and I be perfect objects of D(O_X) [def-pc-derived-category, def-pc-perfect-complex], and let E be any object of D(O_X) [def-pc-derived-category]. The derived tensor-Hom adjunction [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] gives a natural bijection Hom_{D(O_X)}(I,RHom(A,E))\cong Hom_{D(O_X)}(A\otimes^L I,E); under it a morphism I\to RHom(A,E) corresponds to a morphism A\otimes^L I\to E.

source.place: Section section-RHom, tensor-Hom adjunction following Lemma cohomology-lemma-RHom-strictly-perfect

proof.text: Apply the derived internal-Hom adjunction [lem-sc-derived-internal-hom-adjunction] to X and the objects K=I, L=A, M=E, in its symmetric form: it gives a bijection Hom_{D(O_X)}(I,RHom(A,E))\cong Hom_{D(O_X)}(A\otimes^L I,E), functorial in I, A, E. The adjunction holds for all objects of D(O_X); the perfectness of A and I is not used.

source.place: Cohomology Lemma cohomology-lemma-internal-hom (Tag 08DJ), equation (1); Cohomology Lemma cohomology-lemma-symmetric-monoidal-derived (Tag 0FPB)

proof.text: Evaluating the bifunctorial bijection at a morphism gives exactly the stated correspondence between I\to RHom(A,E) and A\otimes^L I\to E.
